messages.author: 598eae3a5857142f
messages.subject: A few million values on x-axis
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to plot a chart that has 3.8 million entries on the x-
axis. The y-axis only has 20 distinct ones.
I tried to simply plot the matrix, which I read through csv. Two
columns, first is a counter column (1:3800000), second has the y-axis
values.

Plotting it in matlab takes less than a second. With ggplot2 it
doesn't seem to finish at all.
What am I doing wrong here?

data <- read.csv("cat.txt")
p <- ggplot(data,aes(x=x,y=y)) + geom_line(colour=lcolor)
print(p)

Data looks like this:
x,y
1,1
2,1
3,1
4,2
5,4
....

Thank in advance ;)

Thomas

messages.author: 7a5c2ea68524e713
messages.subject: Re: A few million values on x-axis
parts:
Dear Thomas,

Not knowing anything about your data I can produce a black rectangle in 11 s
from a 1/40 of your data size.

> x <- 1 : 1e5
> y <- sample (1:20, length (x), replace = TRUE)
> system.time (plot (x, y, type = "l"))
user system elapsed
4.080 0.020 4.097
> p <- ggplot(data.frame (x = x, y = y),aes(x=x,y=y)) + geom_line()
> system.time (print (p))
user system elapsed
10.59 0.03 10.65

However, plotting 4e6 values along x means some thousand values compressed into
one screen pixel. So: if you don't have a kind of structure on that scale,
you're not going to see anything with the line approach.
=> in that case: you need to compute some summary statistic (tiles, running
average, ...). Without knowing what your data means, no one can tell what does
make sense and what doesn't.

If the data is (somewhat) sorted, you can use rle()
y <- sort (y)

> system.time ({
+ yr <- rle (y)
+ data <- data.frame (x = c (0, cumsum (yr$lengths)),
+ y = c (1, yr$values))
+ p <- ggplot(data,aes(x=x,y=y)) + geom_step(direction = "vh")
+ print (p)
+ })
user system elapsed
0.960 0.000 0.973

HTH,

Claudia

As Claudia said, we don't have your data and so it is hard to say what
you expect to get from this plot. So what you may be doing wrong is
trying to plot 3.8 million points/line segments.

> > data <- read.csv("cat.txt")
> > p <- ggplot(data,aes(x=x,y=y)) + geom_line(colour=lcolor)
> > print(p)
>
> > Data looks like this:
> > x,y
> > 1,1
> > 2,1
> > 3,1
> > 4,2
> > 5,4
> > ....

There is no lcolor in your example data. So for my tests, I switched
to geom_point(). Instead of a rectangle, I got 20 effectively solid
lines across the plot.

tim <- function(n) {
data <- data.frame(x=1:n, y=sample(1:20, n, replace=TRUE))
print(system.time(p <- ggplot(data, aes(x=x,y=y)) + geom_point()))
print(system.time(print(p)))
}

tim(3800)
# user system elapsed
# 0.01 0.00 0.02
# user system elapsed
# 1.83 0.08 1.91
tim(38000)
# user system elapsed
# 0.00 0.02 0.02
# user system elapsed
# 4.02 0.48 4.50
tim(380000)
# user system elapsed
# 0.04 0.00 0.04
# user system elapsed
# 30.58 4.39 34.97
tim(3800000)
# user system elapsed
# 0.25 0.14 0.39
#Error: cannot allocate vector of size 29.0 Mb
#In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see
the first 50)
#Timing stopped at: 347.13 15.63 362.91

The vast majority of the time is spent putting the plot on the screen,
not in creating the plot structure. Also, my machine was not even
able to make a plot with 3.8 million points.

As Claudia said, think about what you want the plot to show, and then
summarize the data to show that particular aspect.

parts:
One thing I noticed (with 10x less data) is that Grid's polyline and
segments are much faster than ggplot2 at drawing. Below is a
comparison with and without grouping. It seems the slowdown is due to
the calculations prior to drawing.

baptiste


N <- 1e5
d <- data.frame(x=seq(1,N), y=rnorm(N), id=rep(seq(1,N/2),each=2))

## version for segments
xx <- rep(d$x, each=2)[-c(1, 2*N)]
yy <- rep(d$y, each=2)[-c(1, 2*N)]
start <- seq(1, by=2, length(xx)) # starting points
end <- seq(2, by=2, length(yy)) # end points

d2 <- data.frame(x0=xx[start], x1=xx[end],
y0=yy[start], y1=yy[end],
id=rep(seq(1,N-1),each=2))

## drawing

p1 <- qplot(x,y,data=d,geom="line")
p2 <- p1 + aes(group=id)

g1 <- with(d, polylineGrob(x/N, y/2))
g2 <- with(d, polylineGrob(x/N, y/2, id=id))
g3 <- with(d2, segmentsGrob(x0/N,y0/2,x1/N,y1/2, gp=gpar(col=id)))

png()
system.time(print(p1))
system.time(print(p2))
grid.newpage()
system.time(grid.draw(g1))
grid.newpage()
system.time(grid.draw(g2))
grid.newpage()
system.time(grid.draw(g3))
dev.off()

## user system elapsed
## 9.657 1.118 11.022
## > user system elapsed
## 117.253 23.795 144.114
## > > user system elapsed
## 0.729 0.009 0.753
## > > user system elapsed
## 0.849 0.019 0.885
## > > user system elapsed
## 3.094 0.018 3.134
